response.sql:
WITH filtered AS (
  SELECT orderslink, rebtotal, rebrate / NULLIF(feerate, 0) AS ratio
  FROM fees
  WHERE rebrate > 0.0005 AND orderslink IS NOT NULL
),
per_order AS (
  SELECT orderslink, AVG(rebtotal) AS avg_rebtotal, AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio
  FROM filtered
  GROUP BY orderslink
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS mean_ratio FROM per_order
)
SELECT p.orderslink, p.avg_rebtotal, p.avg_ratio, p.avg_ratio / NULLIF(o.mean_ratio, 0) AS relative_ratio
FROM per_order p
CROSS JOIN overall o
ORDER BY relative_ratio DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Fee rows with a NULL orderslink are excluded because they do not belong to any order. The request does not say how to treat them.

A feerate of 0 or NULL makes the ratio NULL (via NULLIF), so AVG ignores it rather than raising a division error. A NULL or zero overall mean makes relative_ratio NULL, which satisfies the 'provided the mean is not missing' condition. NULLS LAST requires PostgreSQL or SQLite 3.30+.
